title: Tenant traffic containment and noisy neighbor mitigation - PRD (wip)
content:
Summary:
This PRD proposes a combined set of mechanisms—Traffic Containment (TC), Dynamic Tenant Shaping (DTS), and Burst Escrow—to reduce noisy neighbor incidents and improve predictable latency and cost for Dedicated pools. The goal is an operationally simple, predictable set of controls that slots into existing Dedicated autoscaling and quota subsystems while enabling graceful degradation and transparent billing signals to customers.

Problem statement:
- We observe intermittent tenant-level tail latency spikes and capacity contention that manifest as noisy-neighbor incidents: one tenant's burst (batch embedding jobs, bulk reranks, or misconfigured clients) can cause latency SLO violations for co-tenants.
- Current isolation is coarse (pool-level reservations + ad-hoc throttles). When contention occurs, reactive preemption and manual ops intervention are common.
- Customers want stronger guarantees (latency SLOs, predictable reserved throughput) without losing burstability for spiky workloads.

Objectives (success metrics):
- Reduce multi-tenant SLO incident rate in Dedicated pools by 60% in first 90 days post-rollout.
- Limit end-to-end p95 request latency variance per-model to <30% over baseline during concurrent bursts.
- Provide per-tenant burst budget visibility and explainable degradations in Console.
- Keep implementation risk low: no changes to model kernels or customer workload instrumentation required.

Non-goals:
- This PRD does not change base pricing model; billing specifics are handled as follow-on.
- Not proposing wholesale pool redesign or new hypervisor-level isolation.

Constraints and assumptions:
- Dedicated pools remain multi-tenant by default unless reserved slices are purchased.
- We can add lightweight runtime request metering and per-tenant bookkeeping in the control plane.
- Autoscaler will continue to operate; new controls must be compatible with existing scale-up/scale-down signals.

Proposed components (overview):
1) Traffic Containment (TC) - request-level shaping and per-route caps
   - Per-tenant per-route 'soft caps' measured as QPS and token-rate (tokens = model input tokens + generated tokens). Soft caps are configured per-tenant based on reservation level.
   - When a tenant exceeds soft cap, requests are shaped (throttled) into a token-aware queue with controlled release to prevent head-of-line blocking for others.
   - Hard caps exist as emergency guardrails when pool-level capacity is exceeded; hard caps trigger immediate circuit-breaker fallback responses (HTTP 429 + structured reason).

2) Dynamic Tenant Shaping (DTS) - adaptive allocation inside pools
   - Lightweight per-tenant pacing controller that dynamically reduces allotment for noisy tenants based on short-window (30s–2m) contribution to token consumption and latency impact.
   - The DTS controller uses two signals: contribution-to-p95 (how much a tenant's requests pushed p95) and token-imbalance (difference between expected and observed token consumption).
   - Shaping actions: request-level pacing, priority reweighting, and soft downgrade to cheaper compatible model variants (if customer configured fallback).

3) Burst Escrow & Credit Pooling
   - Tenants accrue burst credits proportional to their reservation and payment tier. Credits sit in an escrow that can be spent for short high-throughput bursts.
   - Credits are deducted by token-consumption. When escrow is exhausted, tenant falls back to soft cap behavior (DTS shaping).
   - Admins can configure emergency top-ups (manual or via policy) and configure maximum single-burst size.

4) Noisy-Neighbor Detector (NND) + Alerting
   - Statistical detector that flags tenants with anomalous token variance, sudden p95 contributions, or sustained CPU/GPU utilization spikes correlating to tenant traffic.
   - Integration with Console to show flagged tenants, suspected root cause (e.g., embedding bulk job), and recommended actions (backoff, schedule off-peak, purchase more capacity).

Integration with Autoscaler and Rollout Behavior:
- Autoscaler reacts to pool-level throughput/queueing as before. When TC/DTS observes a tenant hitting caps frequently, telemetry surfaces to autoscaler as candidate for prewarming or suggesting reservation upgrades.
- To avoid oscillation: DTS applies conservative dampening; escalation to preemption or hard caps only after multi-window confirmation.

Operational modes (examples):
- Normal: Tenants operate below soft caps. Autoscaler scales normally.
- Burst with credits: Tenant uses escrow and experiences no shaping until credits approach zero.
- Sustained noisy tenant: DTS progressively shapes traffic, reweights priority, and surfaces to ops; preemption/hard cap only if pool-level SLOs are threatened.

Console & Product UX:
- New Console surfaces: per-tenant credit balance, recent shaping events, and expected time to recovery at current rates.
- Alerts: automatic severity-labeled incidents (info/warn/critical) depending on pool impact.
- Explanations: structured reasons with links to suggested Jira/GitHub runbooks for common root causes.

API/Config model (high-level):
- tenant.config.allowed_soft_cap_tokens_per_minute: integer
- tenant.config.burst_escrow_quota: integer (tokens)
- tenant.config.fallback_model: model-id (optional)
- policies: global pool defaults, per-tenant overrides, emergency_topup_policy

Acceptance criteria (engineering):
- Runtime changes are deployable behind a feature flag per-region.
- End-to-end tests that simulate bursty tenants and assert no more than X% p95 regression for co-tenants.
- Load test harness exercises escrow depletion, DTS shaping, and hard cap enforcement.

Monitoring and SLOs:
- New metrics: tenant_token_rate, tenant_p95_contrib, tenant_credit_balance, shaping_events_count, hardcap_hits.
- Dashboards: per-pool heatmap of token variance and active shaping.
- Pager thresholds: pool-level p95 > configured SLO for N minutes -> oncall paging.

Runbook (high-level):
- Detection: NND flags tenant -> runbook suggests rapid mitigation: disable offending route, throttle client, or move workload to dedicated slice.
- Soft resolution: increase escrow (if on paid plan) or contact solutions engineering for suggested reservation changes.
- Emergency: if pool-level SLOs are impacted, ops may temporarily evict or hard-cap tenant traffic with explicit audit and customer comms.

Risks and mitigations:
- False positives (legitimate high-traffic jobs flagged): provide clear appeals path and allow manual override for verified workloads.
- Complexity in billing/credits: separate billing/quotas project to design transparent UX before wide rollout.
- Autoscaler interaction causing unnecessary scaling: add conservative hysteresis in DTS signals forwarded to autoscaler.

Open questions / next steps:
- Exact credit accrual model: upfront reserve-based vs continuous earn rate? (engineering + finance trade study)
- How to expose shaping decisions to customers in a privacy-preserving way?
- Do we require per-model fallbacks (customers opt-in) for soft downgrades or offer default compatible downgrades?

Milestones (proposed):
- M0 (4w): design review, detector prototype, API schema finalized.
- M1 (8w): implement TC + basic DTS with feature flag; internal load tests.
- M2 (12w): implement Burst Escrow and Console UI; limited alpha with select customers.
- M3 (16–20w): rollout to photos/region-by-region with telemetry-driven adjustments; GA after meeting SLO targets.

Appendix: handy examples and scenarios
- Scenario A (embedding vendor spike): tenant A runs a bulk embed over 5 minutes consuming 10x usual tokens. With escrow it finishes quickly and logs a debit; without escrow DTS shapes it to protect co-tenants.
- Scenario B (misconfigured client): tenant B enters a hot loop, NND flags anomalous token variance; shape applied, ops alerted, tenant notified with suggested mitigation link.

Notes to reviewers:
- This draft focuses on low-risk, control-plane-first approach. Looking for feedback from infra (autoscaler interplay), serving-runtime (efficient token accounting), and finance (credit economics).
- Please add cross-links to related PRDs (capacity-reservoir work, quota-ledger) and surface any overlap that blocks implementation.

(End of draft)
